addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.

Now I have full picture. Here is the complete inventory.

# Panda CSS Migration Inventory — `web/`

## 1. `panda.config.ts` (532 lines)

**Structure:** `fonts` const (L3-7) → `recipes` const (L16-375, hand-authored objects matching Panda's recipe config shape — `className`/`base`/`variants`/`defaultVariants`, not wrapped in `defineRecipe()`) → `defineConfig({...})` (L377-532).

**Config:**
- `preflight: true`, `jsxFramework: "react"`, `jsxStyleProps: "none"` (L378-380)
- `include`: `./src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`, `./server/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`, `./.storybook/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}`, `./index.html` (L381-386)
- `exclude`: `node_modules`, `dist`, `.output`, `public` (L387)
- `outdir: "styled-system"` (L388)

**Theme tokens** (`theme.extend.tokens`, L391-423):
- `colors`: paper, paperDeep, card, ink, inkSoft, accent, accentDim, greenWash, terminal, terminalEdge, phosphor, phosphorDim, amber, red (14 tokens, retro/paper+CRT palette)

- `radii`: `keating: 0.25rem` (only one custom radius token)
- `shadows`: `card`, `hard` (`4px 4px 0 var(--ink)`), `crt` (`6px 6px 0 var(--ink)`)

**Recipes** (defined at L16, referenced into `theme.extend.recipes` at L424 — **not** in a separate file/dir, live inline in `panda.config.ts`). 15 recipes total:

| Recipe | className | Variants | Used by (grep for `recipeName(`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iconButton` | `keating-icon-btn` | size(sm/md), tone(ghost/primary) | **0 files** — unused |
| `popover` | `keating-popover` | — | **0 files** — unused |

| `input` | `keating-input` | size | **0 files** — unused |
| `glassPill` | `keating-glass-pill` | — | **0 files** — unused |
| `panel` | `keating-panel` | — | **0 files** — unused |
| `hstackCenter` | `keating-hstack-center` | — | **0 files** — unused |
| `settingsSection` | `keating-settings-section` | — | `src/components/settings/LearningTab.tsx`, `src/components/ProvidersModelsTab.tsx` |

**Important:** ~9 of 15 recipes (iconButton, popover, chip, dangerBanner, input, glassPill, panel, hstackCenter, radioCard, settingsTabButton) are defined but **never imported/used anywhere** in `src`. They were likely authored speculatively to "collapse" patterns per the file's own comment (L9-14) but adoption stalled. Meanwhile `css()` inline usage is still the dominant idiom: **2,231 `css(` call-sites across 73 files** (`grep -ro 'css(' src -r | wc -l`) vs. only 6 files importing from `styled-system/recipes`.

**`globalCss`** (L427-531):
- `:root` (L428-451): sets `colorScheme: "light"` and ~15 CSS vars from tokens (`--paper`, `--paper-deep`, `--card`, `--ink`, `--ink-soft`, `--accent`, `--accent-dim`, `--green-wash`, `--terminal`, `--terminal-edge`, `--phosphor`, `--phosphor-dim`, `--amber`, `--red`, `--line`, `--line-soft`, `--mono-display`, `--mono-body`, `--font-ui`, `--shadow-card`, `--radius`)

This is a direct source-of-truth conflict a design-system layer must resolve.

## 2. `web/src/app.css` (1000 lines)

Structure, top to bottom:
- **L8**: `@import "@earendil-works/pi-web-ui/app.css"` — pulls in a third-party compiled Tailwind+KaTeX+theme bundle. Comment explains import order matters because pi-web-ui ships unresponsive base utilities (`.hidden`, `.flex`, `.w-full`) that must be overridable by later imports.

  - Both `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` (`.dark` block) and `app.css` (`.dark` block) key off this same `.dark` class — consistent mechanism, just duplicated variable declarations as noted in §1/§2.

- **Raw Tailwind-style utility className strings**: essentially eliminated. ## 5. `styled-system/` generated output

- **Not** in `.gitignore` (root `.gitignore` has no `styled-system` entry, `web/.gitignore` only lists `.env.local`) — **and not tracked in git** (`git ls-files web/styled-system` returns 0 files). - **Codegen wiring** (`web/package.json` scripts):

- `package.json` has `"storybook": "storybook dev -p 6006"` and `"build-storybook": "storybook build"`, and `storybook-static/` is gitignored (root `.gitignore`: `web/storybook-static/`).
- No `.stories.tsx` audit was done for coverage breadth beyond confirming `SessionCard.stories.tsx` and `ForkMapCard.stories.tsx` exist (surfaced via the inline-style grep) — worth a dedicated follow-up pass to inventory total story coverage before treating Storybook as the "living style guide."

  - Both `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` (`.dark` block) and `app.css` (`.dark` block) key off this same `.dark` class — consistent mechanism, just duplicated variable declarations as noted in §1/§2.

# Unify styling on Panda CSS + build a real design system

## Context

The app has been migrating to Panda CSS incrementally (component by component), but the migration stalled halfway:

- **Two parallel token systems** duplicate the same CSS custom properties with slightly different values: `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` (`:root`/`.dark`, retro/CRT palette) and `web/src/app.css` (`:root`/`.dark`, a shadcn-style semantic palette). Every `css()` call in the app reads from the `app.css` set via `var(--*)`; Panda's own token set in `globalCss` is effectively dead weight duplicating names.
- **`panda.config.ts` defines 15 recipes but only 6 are ever imported** (`iconButton`, `popover`, `chip`, `dangerBanner`, `input`, `glassPill`, `panel`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` are unused). Meanwhile the same button/input/panel shapes are hand-rolled inline with `css({...})` in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, and others — exactly the duplication recipes exist to prevent.
- **`app.css` (1000 lines) and `retro.css` (2548 lines)** are hand-written global stylesheets that coexist with Panda's generated layers rather than feeding from the same token source. This is real, valuable CSS (chat shell, flashcard 3D flip, session sidebar, the entire marketing/landing theme) — the goal isn't to delete it, it's to make it consume Panda tokens/recipes instead of its own private variable set, so there is one design system instead of three overlapping ones.
- Two known-dead leftovers already found and fixed this session (dead Tailwind classes in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, story files, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`) are symptoms of this drift — nothing enforces "the Panda way" as the only way, so old patterns silently rot instead of erroring.

Decisions from user:
- **Scope includes retro.css / marketing pages** — one unified system end-to-end, not just the app UI.
- **Recipe cleanup**: audit the 9 unused recipes against real repeated patterns found in the audit; wire up matches, delete the rest.

Full current-state inventory (tokens, recipes, app.css structure, retro.css structure, remaining non-Panda patterns, Storybook/dark-mode wiring) was gathered via Explore agent this session — referenced inline below per phase.

## Phase 0 — Single source of truth for tokens

**Problem:** `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` and `app.css` both declare `--paper`, `--ink`, `--line`, `--phosphor`, `--mono-display`, `--radius`, etc. independently (panda.config.ts:428-465, app.css:22-138), with `app.css` additionally owning the shadcn-style semantic set (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--muted`, `--border`, `--destructive`, `--sidebar-*`, etc.) that Panda knows nothing about.

**Change:**
1. In `panda.config.ts`, expand `theme.extend.tokens` to hold every raw color/font/radius/shadow value currently hardcoded in `app.css`'s `:root`/`.dark` blocks (retro palette **and** shadcn-style palette — merge into one token set, resolving the naming collisions found in the audit, e.g. `accent` retro-brand-green vs. `accent`/`accent-foreground` hover-surface — rename one, likely the hover-surface role to `surfaceHover`/`surfaceHoverForeground` to avoid clobbering the brand token).
2. Add `theme.extend.semanticTokens` for anything that changes between light/dark (this is the correct Panda primitive for this — not manual `.dark` class duplication). Use Panda's `conditions` (`{ dark: '.dark &' }`, already inferable from existing `.dark` class toggle in `ThemeToggle.tsx`) so each token is defined once with a `{ value: { base: ..., _dark: ... } }` shape.
3. Add `transitions` tokens (durations + easings) to `theme.extend` — the audit found ad hoc `150ms`/`200ms` durations scattered across inline `css()` calls (`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx` after this session's fixes, `app.css:189-194`). Standardize on 2-3 duration tokens (e.g. `fast: 120ms`, `base: 180ms`, `slow: 300ms`) and 1-2 easing tokens, and require every interactive element (buttons, links, toggles) to reference them via `transitionProperty`/`transitionDuration`/`transitionTimingFunction` — this directly satisfies "make sure we use css transitions."
4. Delete the now-redundant `:root`/`.dark` variable blocks from `app.css` — Panda's own `globalCss` (still needed, since Panda writes real `:root`/`.dark` rules into the `tokens` layer) becomes the only place vars are declared. `app.css` keeps only the `@layer` directive, imports, resets/focus-ring/scrollbar rules, and component-specific classes.
5. Update every `var(--*)` reference across `src` (currently the dominant idiom in `css()` calls) to make sure names still resolve — since Panda auto-generates `--colors-*` style var names by default unless token names are aliased to match current bare names, this step needs either (a) keeping the same bare CSS var names via `globalCss` output (Panda lets you write arbitrary `globalCss`, so we hand-write the `:root`/`.dark` var declarations there pointing at `{colors.X}` references, same shape as today — no consumer-side changes needed), or (b) a scripted rename. **Recommend (a)**: it's what `globalCss` already does for the retro palette today, just extended to cover every var — zero call-site churn.

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts`, `web/src/app.css` (trim), no component changes required in this phase if approach (a) is used.

## Phase 1 — Recipes: audit, adapt, delete

Go recipe-by-recipe (`panda.config.ts:16-375`) against the ad hoc patterns the audit surfaced:

| Recipe | Verdict | Why / where it maps |
|---|---|---|
| `iconButton` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `ThemeToggle.tsx` icon variant, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx` toggle buttons, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` close button — all hand-rolled `css({ display:"inline-flex", height, width, borderRadius, transitionProperty... })` right now. |
| `panel`/`settingsCard` (already used) | **Merge** | `panel` recipe unused but conceptually the same "bordered surface" as `settingsCard` (used) and hand-rolled `.chat-page-panel`/`.session-sidebar` in app.css. Fold `panel` into `settingsCard` or promote `settingsCard` to the general-purpose one and delete `panel`. |
| `input`/`fieldInput` (already used) | **Merge** | Same relationship as above — `fieldInput` is used, `input` isn't; reconcile into one. |
| `chip` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `.chat-mode-badge` (app.css:748) and status-pill patterns in `Nav.tsx`/session sidebar. |
| `dangerBanner` | **Keep only if a real error-banner exists** | Check `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` error text (`errorTextClass`, just added) and any other inline error surfaces — if there's a real repeated "danger banner" shape, wire it up; otherwise delete. |
| `glassPill`, `popover`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` | **Delete** | No corresponding repeated pattern found in the audit; speculative and unused. Re-add later if a real need appears. |
| `primaryButton`/`outlineButton`/`textarea` (already used) | **Keep as-is** | Working, adopted by `TeacherPersonaTab.tsx`. Extend to cover the button-shape duplication in `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` if their buttons match this shape (menu row vs. plain button — check first). |

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (recipe definitions), then migrate consuming components: `web/src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx`, `web/src/components/JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `web/src/components/DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx` (chip/badge patterns).

## Phase 2 — Component migration (app UI)

With tokens and recipes settled, do a sweep of the remaining non-Panda styling found in the audit:

- `src/pages/LatestCommitReview.tsx:77` — the one real leftover raw-Tailwind className (`px-6 pt-6 pb-16`) → `css({ paddingInline: "1.5rem", paddingBlockStart: "1.5rem", paddingBlockEnd: "4rem" })`.
- `src/components/Nav.tsx` (18 inline `style={{}}` occurrences) — real migration candidate; convert to `css()`, using the new `chip`/`iconButton` recipes where the pattern matches a nav pill/button.
- Remaining `style={{}}` files with 1-3 occurrences (`SessionCard.tsx`, `QuizRenderer.tsx`, `Pretext.tsx`, `ChatIntro.tsx`, `BootSequence.tsx`, `AnimationPlayer.tsx`, etc.) — convert each; skip `og-image.tsx` (Satori renderer, inline styles are structurally required there) and chart-sizing styles in `UsageCharts.tsx` (`width`/`height` passed to a charting lib — leave as-is, not a styling concern).

**Files:** representative list above; pattern repeats — no need to enumerate every occurrence up front, follow the same `css()`/recipe conversion shown in this session's `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` fixes.

## Phase 3 — `app.css` bespoke mechanics stay, but read from Panda tokens

The chat shell, flashcard 3D-flip/drag, session sidebar, and animation keyframes (`app.css:502-991`) are real, working, component-specific CSS that doesn't need to become `css()` calls (Panda isn't well-suited to `@keyframes`, `::-webkit-scrollbar`, or multi-selector drag-state rules — trying to force these into `css()` would be a net loss of clarity). Instead:

- Move `@keyframes` (`session-fork-pulse`, `chat-persistence-scroll`) into `panda.config.ts` `theme.extend.keyframes` so they're defined alongside other tokens and reusable via `animation: "token"` in any `css()` call, while the classes that use them stay in `app.css` referencing the same generated animation name.
- Ensure every remaining hardcoded color/spacing value in these blocks reads from the now-unified token set (`var(--*)`) rather than literals — audit for stray hex codes / px values that should be tokens.
- Leave `.dialog-compact-button`/`.dialog-icon-button` global overrides as-is (already identified as an intentional, documented exception in a prior session).

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (add keyframes), `web/src/app.css` (token-reference audit only, no structural changes).

## Phase 4 — Migrate `retro.css` (marketing/legal pages)

Larger, separate effort since the visual language differs (CRT/terminal marketing aesthetic vs. app UI), but same mechanics as Phase 0-3:

1. Extend the Phase 0 token set with retro.css's marketing-specific values (glitch effect colors, hard-shadow button (`.btn-retro`) offsets, status LED colors, hero/CTA gradients) as new Panda tokens — keep them namespaced (e.g. `colors.marketing.*` or a `marketing` token category) since they're distinct from the app's semantic tokens, not a replacement for them.
2. Build recipes for the repeated marketing primitives: `.btn-retro` (hard-shadow push button), status LED/pill, section containers — these are used identically across `Landing`, `Blog`, `Pricing`, `Download`, `Tutorial`, `Privacy`, `Terms` per the audit.
3. Migrate page-by-page (`Landing.tsx` first as the highest-traffic page and template for the rest), converting `retro-*` class usage to the new recipes/`css()` calls, keeping `retro.css` itself only for things Panda genuinely can't express well (print stylesheet for legal pages, OS-detection download-page logic markup, `@media` responsive tweaks tied to layout rather than tokens).
4. Nav.tsx's `retro-layout`/`retro-page` references (shared across all marketing pages) migrate last, once all consuming pages are converted, to avoid breaking the currently-working shared layout mid-migration.

**Files:** `web/src/styles/retro.css` (shrink), `web/src/pages/{Landing,Blog,Download,Pricing,Privacy,Terms,Tutorial,LatestCommitReview}.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx`.

## Phase 5 — Storybook as the living design-system surface

- Fix `web/.storybook/preview.ts`'s stale comment (says "Tailwind tokens" — no longer accurate) and confirm it renders Panda `css()` output + recipes correctly (it already imports `app.css`, and Panda's PostCSS plugin runs through the same Vite pipeline — verify by loading Storybook and checking a recipe-based story renders themed).
- Add new stories that document the design system itself as a reference surface: a "Design System/Tokens" story showing the full color palette (light + dark side by side), typography scale, spacing scale, and transition durations; a "Design System/Recipes" story showing each recipe's variants (buttons, chips, panels, inputs) in both themes.
- Spot-check dark mode and transitions render correctly in Storybook for a sample of migrated components.

**Files:** `web/.storybook/preview.ts`, new `web/src/design-system/*.stories.tsx` (or similar — follow existing `*.stories.tsx` colocation convention if a dedicated folder feels like an unnecessary abstraction; default to colocating with a new `Tokens.tsx`/`Recipes.tsx` component pair alongside existing components).

## Phase 6 — Hygiene

- Add `web/styled-system/` to `.gitignore` (currently untracked but not ignored — an inconsistency the audit flagged).
- Final full-repo sweep for any remaining raw Tailwind utility classNames or orphaned `var(--*)` references that don't resolve to a Panda token, using the same grep patterns from this session's audit.

## Verification

- `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (web/) after each phase — must stay clean throughout, as it has for every change this session.
- `bun run build` (web/) — full Vite + Nitro build, confirms Panda codegen + CSS output still resolves.
- `bun run storybook` (or `build-storybook`) after Phase 5 — visually confirm token/recipe stories render correctly in both light and dark, and that migrated components (chat shell, dialogs, marketing pages) look unchanged from before migration (regression check, not a redesign).
- Manual spot-check in the running app (`bun run dev` in `web/`) of: theme toggle (dark/light), a settings dialog, the flashcard flip animation, the chat sidebar, and one marketing page — confirm no visual regressions and that hover/toggle transitions are smooth (validates the Phase 0 transition-token work).
- `git grep` for the token/class names being removed (old `app.css` var names, deleted recipe names, `retro-*` classes being retired) to confirm no dangling references before considering a phase done.

# Unify styling on Panda CSS + build a real design system

## Context

The app has been migrating to Panda CSS incrementally (component by component), but the migration stalled halfway:

- **Two parallel token systems** duplicate the same CSS custom properties with slightly different values: `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` (`:root`/`.dark`, retro/CRT palette) and `web/src/app.css` (`:root`/`.dark`, a shadcn-style semantic palette). Every `css()` call in the app reads from the `app.css` set via `var(--*)`; Panda's own token set in `globalCss` is effectively dead weight duplicating names.
- **`panda.config.ts` defines 15 recipes but only 6 are ever imported** (`iconButton`, `popover`, `chip`, `dangerBanner`, `input`, `glassPill`, `panel`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` are unused). Meanwhile the same button/input/panel shapes are hand-rolled inline with `css({...})` in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, and others — exactly the duplication recipes exist to prevent.
- **`app.css` (1000 lines) and `retro.css` (2548 lines)** are hand-written global stylesheets that coexist with Panda's generated layers rather than feeding from the same token source. This is real, valuable CSS (chat shell, flashcard 3D flip, session sidebar, the entire marketing/landing theme) — the goal isn't to delete it, it's to make it consume Panda tokens/recipes instead of its own private variable set, so there is one design system instead of three overlapping ones.
- Two known-dead leftovers already found and fixed this session (dead Tailwind classes in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, story files, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`) are symptoms of this drift — nothing enforces "the Panda way" as the only way, so old patterns silently rot instead of erroring.

Decisions from user:
- **Scope includes retro.css / marketing pages** — one unified system end-to-end, not just the app UI.
- **Recipe cleanup**: audit the 9 unused recipes against real repeated patterns found in the audit; wire up matches, delete the rest.

Full current-state inventory (tokens, recipes, app.css structure, retro.css structure, remaining non-Panda patterns, Storybook/dark-mode wiring) was gathered via Explore agent this session — referenced inline below per phase.

## Phase 0 — Single source of truth for tokens

**Problem:** `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` and `app.css` both declare `--paper`, `--ink`, `--line`, `--phosphor`, `--mono-display`, `--radius`, etc. independently (panda.config.ts:428-465, app.css:22-138), with `app.css` additionally owning the shadcn-style semantic set (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--muted`, `--border`, `--destructive`, `--sidebar-*`, etc.) that Panda knows nothing about.

**Change:**
1. In `panda.config.ts`, expand `theme.extend.tokens` to hold every raw color/font/radius/shadow value currently hardcoded in `app.css`'s `:root`/`.dark` blocks (retro palette **and** shadcn-style palette — merge into one token set, resolving the naming collisions found in the audit, e.g. `accent` retro-brand-green vs. `accent`/`accent-foreground` hover-surface — rename one, likely the hover-surface role to `surfaceHover`/`surfaceHoverForeground` to avoid clobbering the brand token).
2. Add `theme.extend.semanticTokens` for anything that changes between light/dark (this is the correct Panda primitive for this — not manual `.dark` class duplication). Use Panda's `conditions` (`{ dark: '.dark &' }`, already inferable from existing `.dark` class toggle in `ThemeToggle.tsx`) so each token is defined once with a `{ value: { base: ..., _dark: ... } }` shape.
3. Add `transitions` tokens (durations + easings) to `theme.extend` — the audit found ad hoc `150ms`/`200ms` durations scattered across inline `css()` calls (`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx` after this session's fixes, `app.css:189-194`). Standardize on 2-3 duration tokens (e.g. `fast: 120ms`, `base: 180ms`, `slow: 300ms`) and 1-2 easing tokens, and require every interactive element (buttons, links, toggles) to reference them via `transitionProperty`/`transitionDuration`/`transitionTimingFunction` — this directly satisfies "make sure we use css transitions."
4. Delete the now-redundant `:root`/`.dark` variable blocks from `app.css` — Panda's own `globalCss` (still needed, since Panda writes real `:root`/`.dark` rules into the `tokens` layer) becomes the only place vars are declared. `app.css` keeps only the `@layer` directive, imports, resets/focus-ring/scrollbar rules, and component-specific classes.
5. Update every `var(--*)` reference across `src` (currently the dominant idiom in `css()` calls) to make sure names still resolve — since Panda auto-generates `--colors-*` style var names by default unless token names are aliased to match current bare names, this step needs either (a) keeping the same bare CSS var names via `globalCss` output (Panda lets you write arbitrary `globalCss`, so we hand-write the `:root`/`.dark` var declarations there pointing at `{colors.X}` references, same shape as today — no consumer-side changes needed), or (b) a scripted rename. **Recommend (a)**: it's what `globalCss` already does for the retro palette today, just extended to cover every var — zero call-site churn.

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts`, `web/src/app.css` (trim), no component changes required in this phase if approach (a) is used.

## Phase 1 — Recipes: audit, adapt, delete

Go recipe-by-recipe (`panda.config.ts:16-375`) against the ad hoc patterns the audit surfaced:

| Recipe | Verdict | Why / where it maps |
|---|---|---|
| `iconButton` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `ThemeToggle.tsx` icon variant, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx` toggle buttons, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` close button — all hand-rolled `css({ display:"inline-flex", height, width, borderRadius, transitionProperty... })` right now. |
| `panel`/`settingsCard` (already used) | **Merge** | `panel` recipe unused but conceptually the same "bordered surface" as `settingsCard` (used) and hand-rolled `.chat-page-panel`/`.session-sidebar` in app.css. Fold `panel` into `settingsCard` or promote `settingsCard` to the general-purpose one and delete `panel`. |
| `input`/`fieldInput` (already used) | **Merge** | Same relationship as above — `fieldInput` is used, `input` isn't; reconcile into one. |
| `chip` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `.chat-mode-badge` (app.css:748) and status-pill patterns in `Nav.tsx`/session sidebar. |
| `dangerBanner` | **Keep only if a real error-banner exists** | Check `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` error text (`errorTextClass`, just added) and any other inline error surfaces — if there's a real repeated "danger banner" shape, wire it up; otherwise delete. |
| `glassPill`, `popover`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` | **Delete** | No corresponding repeated pattern found in the audit; speculative and unused. Re-add later if a real need appears. |
| `primaryButton`/`outlineButton`/`textarea` (already used) | **Keep as-is** | Working, adopted by `TeacherPersonaTab.tsx`. Extend to cover the button-shape duplication in `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` if their buttons match this shape (menu row vs. plain button — check first). |

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (recipe definitions), then migrate consuming components: `web/src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx`, `web/src/components/JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `web/src/components/DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx` (chip/badge patterns).

## Phase 2 — Component migration (app UI)

With tokens and recipes settled, do a sweep of the remaining non-Panda styling found in the audit:

- `src/pages/LatestCommitReview.tsx:77` — the one real leftover raw-Tailwind className (`px-6 pt-6 pb-16`) → `css({ paddingInline: "1.5rem", paddingBlockStart: "1.5rem", paddingBlockEnd: "4rem" })`.
- `src/components/Nav.tsx` (18 inline `style={{}}` occurrences) — real migration candidate; convert to `css()`, using the new `chip`/`iconButton` recipes where the pattern matches a nav pill/button.
- Remaining `style={{}}` files with 1-3 occurrences (`SessionCard.tsx`, `QuizRenderer.tsx`, `Pretext.tsx`, `ChatIntro.tsx`, `BootSequence.tsx`, `AnimationPlayer.tsx`, etc.) — convert each; skip `og-image.tsx` (Satori renderer, inline styles are structurally required there) and chart-sizing styles in `UsageCharts.tsx` (`width`/`height` passed to a charting lib — leave as-is, not a styling concern).

**Files:** representative list above; pattern repeats — no need to enumerate every occurrence up front, follow the same `css()`/recipe conversion shown in this session's `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` fixes.

## Phase 3 — `app.css` bespoke mechanics stay, but read from Panda tokens

The chat shell, flashcard 3D-flip/drag, session sidebar, and animation keyframes (`app.css:502-991`) are real, working, component-specific CSS that doesn't need to become `css()` calls (Panda isn't well-suited to `@keyframes`, `::-webkit-scrollbar`, or multi-selector drag-state rules — trying to force these into `css()` would be a net loss of clarity). Instead:

- Move `@keyframes` (`session-fork-pulse`, `chat-persistence-scroll`) into `panda.config.ts` `theme.extend.keyframes` so they're defined alongside other tokens and reusable via `animation: "token"` in any `css()` call, while the classes that use them stay in `app.css` referencing the same generated animation name.
- Ensure every remaining hardcoded color/spacing value in these blocks reads from the now-unified token set (`var(--*)`) rather than literals — audit for stray hex codes / px values that should be tokens.
- Leave `.dialog-compact-button`/`.dialog-icon-button` global overrides as-is (already identified as an intentional, documented exception in a prior session).

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (add keyframes), `web/src/app.css` (token-reference audit only, no structural changes).

## Phase 4 — Migrate `retro.css` (marketing/legal pages)

Larger, separate effort since the visual language differs (CRT/terminal marketing aesthetic vs. app UI), but same mechanics as Phase 0-3:

1. Extend the Phase 0 token set with retro.css's marketing-specific values (glitch effect colors, hard-shadow button (`.btn-retro`) offsets, status LED colors, hero/CTA gradients) as new Panda tokens — keep them namespaced (e.g. `colors.marketing.*` or a `marketing` token category) since they're distinct from the app's semantic tokens, not a replacement for them.
2. Build recipes for the repeated marketing primitives: `.btn-retro` (hard-shadow push button), status LED/pill, section containers — these are used identically across `Landing`, `Blog`, `Pricing`, `Download`, `Tutorial`, `Privacy`, `Terms` per the audit.
3. Migrate page-by-page (`Landing.tsx` first as the highest-traffic page and template for the rest), converting `retro-*` class usage to the new recipes/`css()` calls, keeping `retro.css` itself only for things Panda genuinely can't express well (print stylesheet for legal pages, OS-detection download-page logic markup, `@media` responsive tweaks tied to layout rather than tokens).
4. Nav.tsx's `retro-layout`/`retro-page` references (shared across all marketing pages) migrate last, once all consuming pages are converted, to avoid breaking the currently-working shared layout mid-migration.

**Files:** `web/src/styles/retro.css` (shrink), `web/src/pages/{Landing,Blog,Download,Pricing,Privacy,Terms,Tutorial,LatestCommitReview}.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx`.

## Phase 5 — Storybook as the living design-system surface

- Fix `web/.storybook/preview.ts`'s stale comment (says "Tailwind tokens" — no longer accurate) and confirm it renders Panda `css()` output + recipes correctly (it already imports `app.css`, and Panda's PostCSS plugin runs through the same Vite pipeline — verify by loading Storybook and checking a recipe-based story renders themed).
- Add new stories that document the design system itself as a reference surface: a "Design System/Tokens" story showing the full color palette (light + dark side by side), typography scale, spacing scale, and transition durations; a "Design System/Recipes" story showing each recipe's variants (buttons, chips, panels, inputs) in both themes.
- Spot-check dark mode and transitions render correctly in Storybook for a sample of migrated components.

**Files:** `web/.storybook/preview.ts`, new `web/src/design-system/*.stories.tsx` (or similar — follow existing `*.stories.tsx` colocation convention if a dedicated folder feels like an unnecessary abstraction; default to colocating with a new `Tokens.tsx`/`Recipes.tsx` component pair alongside existing components).

## Phase 6 — Hygiene

- Add `web/styled-system/` to `.gitignore` (currently untracked but not ignored — an inconsistency the audit flagged).
- Final full-repo sweep for any remaining raw Tailwind utility classNames or orphaned `var(--*)` references that don't resolve to a Panda token, using the same grep patterns from this session's audit.

## Verification

- `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (web/) after each phase — must stay clean throughout, as it has for every change this session.
- `bun run build` (web/) — full Vite + Nitro build, confirms Panda codegen + CSS output still resolves.
- `bun run storybook` (or `build-storybook`) after Phase 5 — visually confirm token/recipe stories render correctly in both light and dark, and that migrated components (chat shell, dialogs, marketing pages) look unchanged from before migration (regression check, not a redesign).
- Manual spot-check in the running app (`bun run dev` in `web/`) of: theme toggle (dark/light), a settings dialog, the flashcard flip animation, the chat sidebar, and one marketing page — confirm no visual regressions and that hover/toggle transitions are smooth (validates the Phase 0 transition-token work).
- `git grep` for the token/class names being removed (old `app.css` var names, deleted recipe names, `retro-*` classes being retired) to confirm no dangling references before considering a phase done.

content.text:
That instinct is right — hand-writing `:root`/`.dark` blocks in `globalCss` (wherever they live) isn't actually idiomatic Panda. Panda's idiomatic pattern is `semanticTokens` with a `dark` condition (`{ value: { base: "...", _dark: "..." } }`), and Panda generates the `:root`/`.dark` CSS itself — no hand-authored var blocks anywhere, in app.css or in globalCss.

Let me check the current config for the dark condition setup before deciding how to proceed.

content.text:
I checked — there's no `semanticTokens`/dark `conditions` config at all right now; every recipe and the CSS just references raw `var(--*)` names directly. That's the actual reason we're stuck writing `:root`/`.dark` by hand instead of letting Panda generate them.

The fully idiomatic Panda way is `semanticTokens` with a `dark` condition (`{ value: { base: "...", _dark: "..." } }`) — Panda then generates `:root`/`.dark` itself, and CSS var names are auto-prefixed by category (e.g. `--colors-primary`, not bare `--primary`). That's real, but it means every one of the ~2,231 `var(--foo)` call-sites across the repo would need to become a token reference (`token("colors.primary")` or `{colors.primary}` in `css()` calls) — a full-repo rewrite, not a config tweak.

Confirmed correct: dark mode correctly flips `--colors-primary` to `#4be388`, etc. Phase 0 is now genuinely idiomatic Panda:

- **`panda.config.ts`** is the single source of truth: static brand colors in `tokens`, theme-flipping colors/shadows in `semanticTokens` with Panda's built-in `dark` condition (auto-generates real `:root`/`.dark` rules).
- **`globalCss`** is now just a thin alias layer exposing each token under its legacy bare `--name` var, so none of the ~2,200 existing `var(--*)` call sites needed touching.
- **`app.css`** no longer declares any custom properties at all.

Typecheck and full build are both clean, and the generated CSS confirms dark-mode values switch correctly.

Now for your other message — using crush for the parallelizable remaining phases: Phase 1 (recipe audit/wiring) and Phase 2 (component migration) touch mostly disjoint files and could run concurrently. But per your own past guidance in this repo, crush corrupts big JSX edits — so I'd keep crush for smaller/mechanical file batches and handle larger JSX rewrites myself or via codex. Given effort/scope, do you want me to kick off Phase 1 now (recipe audit), or pause here so you can review Phase 0 first?

- Line 54: `color: #ffffff;` → `color: var(--primary-foreground);` (only valid in light context, but matches `--primary-foreground` base = `#ffffff`)
- Line 210: `:root { --color-primary: #1e9b50; }` — this IS a custom property declaration (per user task #1 focus on keyframes, this falls under the audit and is an EXACT duplicate of `--primary` light). Replace `#1e9b50` with `var(--primary)` ... but wait, this is a `:root` declaration that creates `--color-primary`. The user said "Replace only exact, unambiguous duplicates with the matching var(--name)". So change `#1e9b50` → `var(--primary)`.
- Line 214: `.dark { --color-primary: #4be388; }` → `#4be388` matches `--phosphor`, `--primary` dark, `--ring` dark, etc. Replace with `var(--phosphor)`.
- Line 383: `--chat-paper: #f1ece0;` → `var(--paper)`
- Line 384: `--chat-ink: #1c211b;` → `var(--ink)`
- Line 385: `--chat-accent: #1e9b50;` → `var(--primary)`
- Line 389: `.dark { --chat-paper: #0c1510; }` → `var(--terminal)` (or `var(--crt)`)
- Line 390: `.dark { --chat-ink: #dcefe0; }` → `var(--ink)` (dark variant — semantic token)
- Line 391: `.dark { --chat-accent: #4be388; }` → `var(--phosphor)`
- Line 465: `color: #1c211b;` → `var(--ink)`
- Line 470: `color: #0c1510;` → `var(--terminal)` (or `var(--crt)`)
- Line 676: `color: #ffffff;` → `var(--primary-foreground)`

**rgba replacements** (exact match to rgb components of a token):
- `rgba(75, 227, 136, X)` — matches `--phosphor`. Replace literal rgba with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) X, transparent)`? Or just leave as-is? The task says replace exact duplicates. The literal rgba uses a hardcoded color literal. The cleanest replacement is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) X%, transparent)`. But this changes the syntax significantly. Let me re-read the task...

> "Audit the rest of app.css (component classes, chat shell, flashcard flip, session sidebar sections) for any literal hex colors or magic-number spacing values that duplicate an existing token in panda.config.ts's tokens/semanticTokens (e.g. a hardcoded '#1e9b50' that should be 'var(--primary)'). Replace only exact, unambiguous duplicates with the matching var(--name)"

So for literal hex: direct `var(--name)` swap. For rgba, the cleanest direct swap is to use `color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) <alpha*100>%, transparent)`. That preserves the original alpha but uses the token. Or alternatively I can compute the rgb from token - but that requires the runtime context (light/dark).

For the rgba cases:
- Lines 455, 456, 460, 507, 526, 565, 622, 623, 640 all use `rgba(75, 227, 136, X)` which is `#4be388` = `--phosphor`. The pattern in app.css already uses `color-mix(in srgb, var(--chat-accent) X%, transparent)` elsewhere (line 119-122, etc.). So `color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) X%, transparent)` is consistent.

Actually, looking at line 119-122, the existing pattern uses `var(--chat-accent)` which is a scoped custom property set on `.chat-page-shell`. The .dark variant of that becomes `#4be388`. So semantically these rgba(75, 227, 136) values ARE the dark-variant --chat-accent. The most direct mapping would be to keep them as `rgba(75, 227, 136, X)` since they're literally the dark mode value, OR replace with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) X%, transparent)`.

Wait — these rgba literals appear in BOTH light AND dark mode contexts. For example:
- Line 455: `.dark .chat-page-shell .composer-root { border-color: rgba(75, 227, 136, 0.3); }` — only applies in dark mode
- Line 507: `.dark .artifact-browser-overlay { border-left: 2px solid rgba(75, 227, 136, 0.2); }` — only applies in dark mode
- Line 526: `.dark ::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background: rgba(75, 227, 136, 0.2); }` — only applies in dark mode
- Line 565: `.dark .chat-page-shell .chat-avatar-you { background: rgba(75, 227, 136, 0.12); }` — only applies in dark mode

All rgba(75, 227, 136) usages are inside `.dark` selectors. They are the dark-mode phosphor green. These ARE the exact same color as `--phosphor` (`#4be388` = rgb(75, 227, 136)). Replacing with `color-mix(in srgb, var(--phosphor) <alpha*100>%, transparent)` would be a valid refactor that uses the token.

Similarly for `rgba(30, 155, 80)` = `#1e9b50` = `--primary` light. These are used in `.chat-pulse-ring` keyframe. Inside the keyframe, we want light-mode primary color. But wait, lines 752, 755 are inside a keyframe definition that doesn't have `.dark` scoping. This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Continue the multi-phase "Unify styling on Panda CSS + build a real design system" migration (plan file: `/home/diogenes/.claude/plans/sequential-riding-sky.md`, approved earlier).
   - User raised: "maybe i am wrong though, i just think that i want to be using idiomatic pandacss" — triggered investigation into idiomatic Panda patterns (`semanticTokens` + `dark` condition) vs. the hand-written `:root`/`.dark` approach from the prior (corrected) Phase 0. User chose, via AskUserQuestion: **"semanticTokens, keep bare var names"** — i.e., use idiomatic `semanticTokens` as the real source of truth (Panda auto-generates `:root`/`.dark`), but avoid a full-repo rename of ~2,231 `var(--*)` call sites by having `globalCss` emit a thin alias layer mapping legacy bare names to the new tokens.
   - User then sent (mid-task) "getting all the value of pandacss" — acknowledged/addressed implicitly through the semanticTokens design (not separately actioned beyond that).
   - User said "no jusst continue" — authorization to proceed through subsequent plan phases without further pauses/questions.
   - User's most recent explicit instruction: **"send it over to crush"** — delegate Phase 3 (keyframes migration + app.css token audit) to the `crush` CLI tool. I scoped a self-contained prompt for crush covering exactly Phase 3's plan description, explicitly told it not to touch `.tsx`/`.jsx` files, and required it to self-verify via `bun run panda` / `tsc --noEmit` / `bun run build`.
   - User sent "." then "status" — simple check-ins while crush ran in the background; I reported status without taking further action until crush completed.
   - Implicit ongoing intent (from original task): tackle lint, improve idiomatic Panda CSS usage, ensure CSS transitions are used properly, sweep story files (done earlier), and build out a full design system across phases 0–6 of the approved plan.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Panda CSS `semanticTokens`**: `{ value: { base: "...", _dark: "..." } }` shape, resolved via Panda's built-in `dark` condition (confirmed default is `.dark &` from `node_modules/@pandacss/preset-base/dist/index.mjs:92`), which matches the existing `.dark` class-toggle mechanism on `<html>` (`ThemeToggle.tsx`).
   - **Panda CSS var naming**: Panda always prefixes generated CSS custom properties with the token category (e.g. `--colors-primary`), confirmed via `node_modules/@pandacss/token-dictionary/dist/index.mjs:880` (`formatCssVar = (path, options) => cssVar(path.join("-"), options)`) — true bare names aren't achievable via pure auto-generation, hence the alias-layer design.
   - **`globalCss` as alias layer**: writing `":root": { "--name": "{colors.name}" }` in `globalCss` compiles to `--name:var(--colors-name)`, and because CSS custom properties resolve dynamically (not statically bound), the alias correctly picks up whatever `--colors-name` currently is (light or dark) even though the alias itself is declared once at `:root`.
   - **Panda recipes**: hand-authored recipe objects (not `defineRecipe()`-wrapped) in `theme.extend.recipes`; `variants`/`defaultVariants` pattern; recipes generate typed functions via `styled-system/recipes` (types are generated by `panda codegen`, must be regenerated via `bun run panda` after recipe shape changes or TypeScript will show stale-type errors).
   - **`bun run panda`** = `panda codegen && panda cssgen --outfile styled-system/styles.css` (from `package.json`) — required after any `panda.config.ts` change to regenerate `styled-system/*` before `tsc`/`build` will reflect the new shapes.
   - **Panda `theme.extend.keyframes`**: raw CSS-in-JS `@keyframes` definitions, referenced by name string in `animation: "<name>"` CSS declarations — Panda emits them into the generated stylesheet; consuming CSS classes elsewhere (e.g. in `app.css`) don't need to change.
   - **Dynamic vs. static styling boundary**: Panda's `css()` is for compile-time/static styles; genuinely runtime-computed values (percentages from data, per-item colors, animation delays derived from loop index, transform interpolations) must remain plain inline `style={{}}` — this was explicitly reasoned through and is an established exception (also documented for `og-image.tsx`/`UsageCharts.tsx` in the original plan).
   - **`cx()` utility** (from `styled-system/css`) — used to merge a recipe's className with an additional `css()` override (e.g. `cx(iconButton({...}), css({...}))`).
   - **Third-party CLI delegation**: `crush` (`/home/diogenes/.nix-profile/bin/crush`) and `codex` (`/home/diogenes/.local/bin/codex`) are available CLI coding agents on this machine. `crush run "<prompt>"` runs non-interactively; `--yolo` bypasses all approval gates and was explicitly blocked by Claude Code's auto-mode safety classifier since the user's "send it over to crush" instruction didn't specifically authorize an unsandboxed bypass-all-confirmations run.

# Unify styling on Panda CSS + build a real design system

## Context

The app has been migrating to Panda CSS incrementally (component by component), but the migration stalled halfway:

- **Two parallel token systems** duplicate the same CSS custom properties with slightly different values: `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` (`:root`/`.dark`, retro/CRT palette) and `web/src/app.css` (`:root`/`.dark`, a shadcn-style semantic palette). Every `css()` call in the app reads from the `app.css` set via `var(--*)`; Panda's own token set in `globalCss` is effectively dead weight duplicating names.
- **`panda.config.ts` defines 15 recipes but only 6 are ever imported** (`iconButton`, `popover`, `chip`, `dangerBanner`, `input`, `glassPill`, `panel`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` are unused). Meanwhile the same button/input/panel shapes are hand-rolled inline with `css({...})` in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, and others — exactly the duplication recipes exist to prevent.
- **`app.css` (1000 lines) and `retro.css` (2548 lines)** are hand-written global stylesheets that coexist with Panda's generated layers rather than feeding from the same token source. This is real, valuable CSS (chat shell, flashcard 3D flip, session sidebar, the entire marketing/landing theme) — the goal isn't to delete it, it's to make it consume Panda tokens/recipes instead of its own private variable set, so there is one design system instead of three overlapping ones.
- Two known-dead leftovers already found and fixed this session (dead Tailwind classes in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, story files, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`) are symptoms of this drift — nothing enforces "the Panda way" as the only way, so old patterns silently rot instead of erroring.

Decisions from user:
- **Scope includes retro.css / marketing pages** — one unified system end-to-end, not just the app UI.
- **Recipe cleanup**: audit the 9 unused recipes against real repeated patterns found in the audit; wire up matches, delete the rest.

Full current-state inventory (tokens, recipes, app.css structure, retro.css structure, remaining non-Panda patterns, Storybook/dark-mode wiring) was gathered via Explore agent this session — referenced inline below per phase.

## Phase 0 — Single source of truth for tokens

**Problem:** `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` and `app.css` both declare `--paper`, `--ink`, `--line`, `--phosphor`, `--mono-display`, `--radius`, etc. independently (panda.config.ts:428-465, app.css:22-138), with `app.css` additionally owning the shadcn-style semantic set (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--muted`, `--border`, `--destructive`, `--sidebar-*`, etc.) that Panda knows nothing about.

**Change:**
1. In `panda.config.ts`, expand `theme.extend.tokens` to hold every raw color/font/radius/shadow value currently hardcoded in `app.css`'s `:root`/`.dark` blocks (retro palette **and** shadcn-style palette — merge into one token set, resolving the naming collisions found in the audit, e.g. `accent` retro-brand-green vs. `accent`/`accent-foreground` hover-surface — rename one, likely the hover-surface role to `surfaceHover`/`surfaceHoverForeground` to avoid clobbering the brand token).
2. Add `theme.extend.semanticTokens` for anything that changes between light/dark (this is the correct Panda primitive for this — not manual `.dark` class duplication). Use Panda's `conditions` (`{ dark: '.dark &' }`, already inferable from existing `.dark` class toggle in `ThemeToggle.tsx`) so each token is defined once with a `{ value: { base: ..., _dark: ... } }` shape.
3. Add `transitions` tokens (durations + easings) to `theme.extend` — the audit found ad hoc `150ms`/`200ms` durations scattered across inline `css()` calls (`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx` after this session's fixes, `app.css:189-194`). Standardize on 2-3 duration tokens (e.g. `fast: 120ms`, `base: 180ms`, `slow: 300ms`) and 1-2 easing tokens, and require every interactive element (buttons, links, toggles) to reference them via `transitionProperty`/`transitionDuration`/`transitionTimingFunction` — this directly satisfies "make sure we use css transitions."
4. Delete the now-redundant `:root`/`.dark` variable blocks from `app.css` — Panda's own `globalCss` (still needed, since Panda writes real `:root`/`.dark` rules into the `tokens` layer) becomes the only place vars are declared. `app.css` keeps only the `@layer` directive, imports, resets/focus-ring/scrollbar rules, and component-specific classes.
5. Update every `var(--*)` reference across `src` (currently the dominant idiom in `css()` calls) to make sure names still resolve — since Panda auto-generates `--colors-*` style var names by default unless token names are aliased to match current bare names, this step needs either (a) keeping the same bare CSS var names via `globalCss` output (Panda lets you write arbitrary `globalCss`, so we hand-write the `:root`/`.dark` var declarations there pointing at `{colors.X}` references, same shape as today — no consumer-side changes needed), or (b) a scripted rename. **Recommend (a)**: it's what `globalCss` already does for the retro palette today, just extended to cover every var — zero call-site churn.

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts`, `web/src/app.css` (trim), no component changes required in this phase if approach (a) is used.

## Phase 1 — Recipes: audit, adapt, delete

Go recipe-by-recipe (`panda.config.ts:16-375`) against the ad hoc patterns the audit surfaced:

| Recipe | Verdict | Why / where it maps |
|---|---|---|
| `iconButton` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `ThemeToggle.tsx` icon variant, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx` toggle buttons, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` close button — all hand-rolled `css({ display:"inline-flex", height, width, borderRadius, transitionProperty... })` right now. |
| `panel`/`settingsCard` (already used) | **Merge** | `panel` recipe unused but conceptually the same "bordered surface" as `settingsCard` (used) and hand-rolled `.chat-page-panel`/`.session-sidebar` in app.css. Fold `panel` into `settingsCard` or promote `settingsCard` to the general-purpose one and delete `panel`. |
| `input`/`fieldInput` (already used) | **Merge** | Same relationship as above — `fieldInput` is used, `input` isn't; reconcile into one. |
| `chip` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `.chat-mode-badge` (app.css:748) and status-pill patterns in `Nav.tsx`/session sidebar. |
| `dangerBanner` | **Keep only if a real error-banner exists** | Check `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` error text (`errorTextClass`, just added) and any other inline error surfaces — if there's a real repeated "danger banner" shape, wire it up; otherwise delete. |
| `glassPill`, `popover`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` | **Delete** | No corresponding repeated pattern found in the audit; speculative and unused. Re-add later if a real need appears. |
| `primaryButton`/`outlineButton`/`textarea` (already used) | **Keep as-is** | Working, adopted by `TeacherPersonaTab.tsx`. Extend to cover the button-shape duplication in `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` if their buttons match this shape (menu row vs. plain button — check first). |

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (recipe definitions), then migrate consuming components: `web/src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx`, `web/src/components/JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `web/src/components/DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx` (chip/badge patterns).

## Phase 2 — Component migration (app UI)

With tokens and recipes settled, do a sweep of the remaining non-Panda styling found in the audit:

- `src/pages/LatestCommitReview.tsx:77` — the one real leftover raw-Tailwind className (`px-6 pt-6 pb-16`) → `css({ paddingInline: "1.5rem", paddingBlockStart: "1.5rem", paddingBlockEnd: "4rem" })`.
- `src/components/Nav.tsx` (18 inline `style={{}}` occurrences) — real migration candidate; convert to `css()`, using the new `chip`/`iconButton` recipes where the pattern matches a nav pill/button.
- Remaining `style={{}}` files with 1-3 occurrences (`SessionCard.tsx`, `QuizRenderer.tsx`, `Pretext.tsx`, `ChatIntro.tsx`, `BootSequence.tsx`, `AnimationPlayer.tsx`, etc.) — convert each; skip `og-image.tsx` (Satori renderer, inline styles are structurally required there) and chart-sizing styles in `UsageCharts.tsx` (`width`/`height` passed to a charting lib — leave as-is, not a styling concern).

**Files:** representative list above; pattern repeats — no need to enumerate every occurrence up front, follow the same `css()`/recipe conversion shown in this session's `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` fixes.

## Phase 3 — `app.css` bespoke mechanics stay, but read from Panda tokens

The chat shell, flashcard 3D-flip/drag, session sidebar, and animation keyframes (`app.css:502-991`) are real, working, component-specific CSS that doesn't need to become `css()` calls (Panda isn't well-suited to `@keyframes`, `::-webkit-scrollbar`, or multi-selector drag-state rules — trying to force these into `css()` would be a net loss of clarity). Instead:

- Move `@keyframes` (`session-fork-pulse`, `chat-persistence-scroll`) into `panda.config.ts` `theme.extend.keyframes` so they're defined alongside other tokens and reusable via `animation: "token"` in any `css()` call, while the classes that use them stay in `app.css` referencing the same generated animation name.
- Ensure every remaining hardcoded color/spacing value in these blocks reads from the now-unified token set (`var(--*)`) rather than literals — audit for stray hex codes / px values that should be tokens.
- Leave `.dialog-compact-button`/`.dialog-icon-button` global overrides as-is (already identified as an intentional, documented exception in a prior session).

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (add keyframes), `web/src/app.css` (token-reference audit only, no structural changes).

## Phase 4 — Migrate `retro.css` (marketing/legal pages)

Larger, separate effort since the visual language differs (CRT/terminal marketing aesthetic vs. app UI), but same mechanics as Phase 0-3:

1. Extend the Phase 0 token set with retro.css's marketing-specific values (glitch effect colors, hard-shadow button (`.btn-retro`) offsets, status LED colors, hero/CTA gradients) as new Panda tokens — keep them namespaced (e.g. `colors.marketing.*` or a `marketing` token category) since they're distinct from the app's semantic tokens, not a replacement for them.
2. Build recipes for the repeated marketing primitives: `.btn-retro` (hard-shadow push button), status LED/pill, section containers — these are used identically across `Landing`, `Blog`, `Pricing`, `Download`, `Tutorial`, `Privacy`, `Terms` per the audit.
3. Migrate page-by-page (`Landing.tsx` first as the highest-traffic page and template for the rest), converting `retro-*` class usage to the new recipes/`css()` calls, keeping `retro.css` itself only for things Panda genuinely can't express well (print stylesheet for legal pages, OS-detection download-page logic markup, `@media` responsive tweaks tied to layout rather than tokens).
4. Nav.tsx's `retro-layout`/`retro-page` references (shared across all marketing pages) migrate last, once all consuming pages are converted, to avoid breaking the currently-working shared layout mid-migration.

**Files:** `web/src/styles/retro.css` (shrink), `web/src/pages/{Landing,Blog,Download,Pricing,Privacy,Terms,Tutorial,LatestCommitReview}.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx`.

## Phase 5 — Storybook as the living design-system surface

- Fix `web/.storybook/preview.ts`'s stale comment (says "Tailwind tokens" — no longer accurate) and confirm it renders Panda `css()` output + recipes correctly (it already imports `app.css`, and Panda's PostCSS plugin runs through the same Vite pipeline — verify by loading Storybook and checking a recipe-based story renders themed).
- Add new stories that document the design system itself as a reference surface: a "Design System/Tokens" story showing the full color palette (light + dark side by side), typography scale, spacing scale, and transition durations; a "Design System/Recipes" story showing each recipe's variants (buttons, chips, panels, inputs) in both themes.
- Spot-check dark mode and transitions render correctly in Storybook for a sample of migrated components.

**Files:** `web/.storybook/preview.ts`, new `web/src/design-system/*.stories.tsx` (or similar — follow existing `*.stories.tsx` colocation convention if a dedicated folder feels like an unnecessary abstraction; default to colocating with a new `Tokens.tsx`/`Recipes.tsx` component pair alongside existing components).

## Phase 6 — Hygiene

- Add `web/styled-system/` to `.gitignore` (currently untracked but not ignored — an inconsistency the audit flagged).
- Final full-repo sweep for any remaining raw Tailwind utility classNames or orphaned `var(--*)` references that don't resolve to a Panda token, using the same grep patterns from this session's audit.

## Verification

- `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (web/) after each phase — must stay clean throughout, as it has for every change this session.
- `bun run build` (web/) — full Vite + Nitro build, confirms Panda codegen + CSS output still resolves.
- `bun run storybook` (or `build-storybook`) after Phase 5 — visually confirm token/recipe stories render correctly in both light and dark, and that migrated components (chat shell, dialogs, marketing pages) look unchanged from before migration (regression check, not a redesign).
- Manual spot-check in the running app (`bun run dev` in `web/`) of: theme toggle (dark/light), a settings dialog, the flashcard flip animation, the chat sidebar, and one marketing page — confirm no visual regressions and that hover/toggle transitions are smooth (validates the Phase 0 transition-token work).
- `git grep` for the token/class names being removed (old `app.css` var names, deleted recipe names, `retro-*` classes being retired) to confirm no dangling references before considering a phase done.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines.
