# Unify styling on Panda CSS + build a real design system

## Context

The app has been migrating to Panda CSS incrementally (component by component), but the migration stalled halfway:

- **Two parallel token systems** duplicate the same CSS custom properties with slightly different values: `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` (`:root`/`.dark`, retro/CRT palette) and `web/src/app.css` (`:root`/`.dark`, a shadcn-style semantic palette). Every `css()` call in the app reads from the `app.css` set via `var(--*)`; Panda's own token set in `globalCss` is effectively dead weight duplicating names.
- **`panda.config.ts` defines 15 recipes but only 6 are ever imported** (`iconButton`, `popover`, `chip`, `dangerBanner`, `input`, `glassPill`, `panel`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` are unused). Meanwhile the same button/input/panel shapes are hand-rolled inline with `css({...})` in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, and others — exactly the duplication recipes exist to prevent.
- **`app.css` (1000 lines) and `retro.css` (2548 lines)** are hand-written global stylesheets that coexist with Panda's generated layers rather than feeding from the same token source. This is real, valuable CSS (chat shell, flashcard 3D flip, session sidebar, the entire marketing/landing theme) — the goal isn't to delete it, it's to make it consume Panda tokens/recipes instead of its own private variable set, so there is one design system instead of three overlapping ones.
- Two known-dead leftovers already found and fixed this session (dead Tailwind classes in `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, story files, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`) are symptoms of this drift — nothing enforces "the Panda way" as the only way, so old patterns silently rot instead of erroring.

Decisions from user:
- **Scope includes retro.css / marketing pages** — one unified system end-to-end, not just the app UI.
- **Recipe cleanup**: audit the 9 unused recipes against real repeated patterns found in the audit; wire up matches, delete the rest.

Full current-state inventory (tokens, recipes, app.css structure, retro.css structure, remaining non-Panda patterns, Storybook/dark-mode wiring) was gathered via Explore agent this session — referenced inline below per phase.

## Phase 0 — Single source of truth for tokens

**Problem:** `panda.config.ts` `globalCss` and `app.css` both declare `--paper`, `--ink`, `--line`, `--phosphor`, `--mono-display`, `--radius`, etc. independently (panda.config.ts:428-465, app.css:22-138), with `app.css` additionally owning the shadcn-style semantic set (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--muted`, `--border`, `--destructive`, `--sidebar-*`, etc.) that Panda knows nothing about.

**Change:**
1. In `panda.config.ts`, expand `theme.extend.tokens` to hold every raw color/font/radius/shadow value currently hardcoded in `app.css`'s `:root`/`.dark` blocks (retro palette **and** shadcn-style palette — merge into one token set, resolving the naming collisions found in the audit, e.g. `accent` retro-brand-green vs. `accent`/`accent-foreground` hover-surface — rename one, likely the hover-surface role to `surfaceHover`/`surfaceHoverForeground` to avoid clobbering the brand token).
2. Add `theme.extend.semanticTokens` for anything that changes between light/dark (this is the correct Panda primitive for this — not manual `.dark` class duplication). Use Panda's `conditions` (`{ dark: '.dark &' }`, already inferable from existing `.dark` class toggle in `ThemeToggle.tsx`) so each token is defined once with a `{ value: { base: ..., _dark: ... } }` shape.
3. Add `transitions` tokens (durations + easings) to `theme.extend` — the audit found ad hoc `150ms`/`200ms` durations scattered across inline `css()` calls (`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx` after this session's fixes, `app.css:189-194`). Standardize on 2-3 duration tokens (e.g. `fast: 120ms`, `base: 180ms`, `slow: 300ms`) and 1-2 easing tokens, and require every interactive element (buttons, links, toggles) to reference them via `transitionProperty`/`transitionDuration`/`transitionTimingFunction` — this directly satisfies "make sure we use css transitions."
4. Delete the now-redundant `:root`/`.dark` variable blocks from `app.css` — Panda's own `globalCss` (still needed, since Panda writes real `:root`/`.dark` rules into the `tokens` layer) becomes the only place vars are declared. `app.css` keeps only the `@layer` directive, imports, resets/focus-ring/scrollbar rules, and component-specific classes.
5. Update every `var(--*)` reference across `src` (currently the dominant idiom in `css()` calls) to make sure names still resolve — since Panda auto-generates `--colors-*` style var names by default unless token names are aliased to match current bare names, this step needs either (a) keeping the same bare CSS var names via `globalCss` output (Panda lets you write arbitrary `globalCss`, so we hand-write the `:root`/`.dark` var declarations there pointing at `{colors.X}` references, same shape as today — no consumer-side changes needed), or (b) a scripted rename. **Recommend (a)**: it's what `globalCss` already does for the retro palette today, just extended to cover every var — zero call-site churn.

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts`, `web/src/app.css` (trim), no component changes required in this phase if approach (a) is used.

## Phase 1 — Recipes: audit, adapt, delete

Go recipe-by-recipe (`panda.config.ts:16-375`) against the ad hoc patterns the audit surfaced:

| Recipe | Verdict | Why / where it maps |
|---|---|---|
| `iconButton` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `ThemeToggle.tsx` icon variant, `JsonCrackBlock.tsx` toggle buttons, `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` close button — all hand-rolled `css({ display:"inline-flex", height, width, borderRadius, transitionProperty... })` right now. |
| `panel`/`settingsCard` (already used) | **Merge** | `panel` recipe unused but conceptually the same "bordered surface" as `settingsCard` (used) and hand-rolled `.chat-page-panel`/`.session-sidebar` in app.css. Fold `panel` into `settingsCard` or promote `settingsCard` to the general-purpose one and delete `panel`. |
| `input`/`fieldInput` (already used) | **Merge** | Same relationship as above — `fieldInput` is used, `input` isn't; reconcile into one. |
| `chip` | **Adapt & wire up** | Matches `.chat-mode-badge` (app.css:748) and status-pill patterns in `Nav.tsx`/session sidebar. |
| `dangerBanner` | **Keep only if a real error-banner exists** | Check `DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` error text (`errorTextClass`, just added) and any other inline error surfaces — if there's a real repeated "danger banner" shape, wire it up; otherwise delete. |
| `glassPill`, `popover`, `hstackCenter`, `radioCard`, `settingsTabButton` | **Delete** | No corresponding repeated pattern found in the audit; speculative and unused. Re-add later if a real need appears. |
| `primaryButton`/`outlineButton`/`textarea` (already used) | **Keep as-is** | Working, adopted by `TeacherPersonaTab.tsx`. Extend to cover the button-shape duplication in `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` if their buttons match this shape (menu row vs. plain button — check first). |

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (recipe definitions), then migrate consuming components: `web/src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx`, `web/src/components/JsonCrackBlock.tsx`, `web/src/components/DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx` (chip/badge patterns).

## Phase 2 — Component migration (app UI)

With tokens and recipes settled, do a sweep of the remaining non-Panda styling found in the audit:

- `src/pages/LatestCommitReview.tsx:77` — the one real leftover raw-Tailwind className (`px-6 pt-6 pb-16`) → `css({ paddingInline: "1.5rem", paddingBlockStart: "1.5rem", paddingBlockEnd: "4rem" })`.
- `src/components/Nav.tsx` (18 inline `style={{}}` occurrences) — real migration candidate; convert to `css()`, using the new `chip`/`iconButton` recipes where the pattern matches a nav pill/button.
- Remaining `style={{}}` files with 1-3 occurrences (`SessionCard.tsx`, `QuizRenderer.tsx`, `Pretext.tsx`, `ChatIntro.tsx`, `BootSequence.tsx`, `AnimationPlayer.tsx`, etc.) — convert each; skip `og-image.tsx` (Satori renderer, inline styles are structurally required there) and chart-sizing styles in `UsageCharts.tsx` (`width`/`height` passed to a charting lib — leave as-is, not a styling concern).

**Files:** representative list above; pattern repeats — no need to enumerate every occurrence up front, follow the same `css()`/recipe conversion shown in this session's `ThemeToggle.tsx`/`JsonCrackBlock.tsx`/`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` fixes.

## Phase 3 — `app.css` bespoke mechanics stay, but read from Panda tokens

The chat shell, flashcard 3D-flip/drag, session sidebar, and animation keyframes (`app.css:502-991`) are real, working, component-specific CSS that doesn't need to become `css()` calls (Panda isn't well-suited to `@keyframes`, `::-webkit-scrollbar`, or multi-selector drag-state rules — trying to force these into `css()` would be a net loss of clarity). Instead:

- Move `@keyframes` (`session-fork-pulse`, `chat-persistence-scroll`) into `panda.config.ts` `theme.extend.keyframes` so they're defined alongside other tokens and reusable via `animation: "token"` in any `css()` call, while the classes that use them stay in `app.css` referencing the same generated animation name.
- Ensure every remaining hardcoded color/spacing value in these blocks reads from the now-unified token set (`var(--*)`) rather than literals — audit for stray hex codes / px values that should be tokens.
- Leave `.dialog-compact-button`/`.dialog-icon-button` global overrides as-is (already identified as an intentional, documented exception in a prior session).

**Files:** `web/panda.config.ts` (add keyframes), `web/src/app.css` (token-reference audit only, no structural changes).

## Phase 4 — Migrate `retro.css` (marketing/legal pages)

Larger, separate effort since the visual language differs (CRT/terminal marketing aesthetic vs. app UI), but same mechanics as Phase 0-3:

1. Extend the Phase 0 token set with retro.css's marketing-specific values (glitch effect colors, hard-shadow button (`.btn-retro`) offsets, status LED colors, hero/CTA gradients) as new Panda tokens — keep them namespaced (e.g. `colors.marketing.*` or a `marketing` token category) since they're distinct from the app's semantic tokens, not a replacement for them.
2. Build recipes for the repeated marketing primitives: `.btn-retro` (hard-shadow push button), status LED/pill, section containers — these are used identically across `Landing`, `Blog`, `Pricing`, `Download`, `Tutorial`, `Privacy`, `Terms` per the audit.
3. Migrate page-by-page (`Landing.tsx` first as the highest-traffic page and template for the rest), converting `retro-*` class usage to the new recipes/`css()` calls, keeping `retro.css` itself only for things Panda genuinely can't express well (print stylesheet for legal pages, OS-detection download-page logic markup, `@media` responsive tweaks tied to layout rather than tokens).
4. Nav.tsx's `retro-layout`/`retro-page` references (shared across all marketing pages) migrate last, once all consuming pages are converted, to avoid breaking the currently-working shared layout mid-migration.

**Files:** `web/src/styles/retro.css` (shrink), `web/src/pages/{Landing,Blog,Download,Pricing,Privacy,Terms,Tutorial,LatestCommitReview}.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx`.

## Phase 5 — Storybook as the living design-system surface

- Fix `web/.storybook/preview.ts`'s stale comment (says "Tailwind tokens" — no longer accurate) and confirm it renders Panda `css()` output + recipes correctly (it already imports `app.css`, and Panda's PostCSS plugin runs through the same Vite pipeline — verify by loading Storybook and checking a recipe-based story renders themed).
- Add new stories that document the design system itself as a reference surface: a "Design System/Tokens" story showing the full color palette (light + dark side by side), typography scale, spacing scale, and transition durations; a "Design System/Recipes" story showing each recipe's variants (buttons, chips, panels, inputs) in both themes.
- Spot-check dark mode and transitions render correctly in Storybook for a sample of migrated components.

**Files:** `web/.storybook/preview.ts`, new `web/src/design-system/*.stories.tsx` (or similar — follow existing `*.stories.tsx` colocation convention if a dedicated folder feels like an unnecessary abstraction; default to colocating with a new `Tokens.tsx`/`Recipes.tsx` component pair alongside existing components).

## Phase 6 — Hygiene

- Add `web/styled-system/` to `.gitignore` (currently untracked but not ignored — an inconsistency the audit flagged).
- Final full-repo sweep for any remaining raw Tailwind utility classNames or orphaned `var(--*)` references that don't resolve to a Panda token, using the same grep patterns from this session's audit.

## Verification

- `bun x tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (web/) after each phase — must stay clean throughout, as it has for every change this session.
- `bun run build` (web/) — full Vite + Nitro build, confirms Panda codegen + CSS output still resolves.
- `bun run storybook` (or `build-storybook`) after Phase 5 — visually confirm token/recipe stories render correctly in both light and dark, and that migrated components (chat shell, dialogs, marketing pages) look unchanged from before migration (regression check, not a redesign).
- Manual spot-check in the running app (`bun run dev` in `web/`) of: theme toggle (dark/light), a settings dialog, the flashcard flip animation, the chat sidebar, and one marketing page — confirm no visual regressions and that hover/toggle transitions are smooth (validates the Phase 0 transition-token work).
- `git grep` for the token/class names being removed (old `app.css` var names, deleted recipe names, `retro-*` classes being retired) to confirm no dangling references before considering a phase done.

content.text:
Clean build, `retro.css` now at 2,242 lines (from 2,548 at Phase 4 start).

**This pass:** merged `.paper-fold` + `.distressed-border` (always used together across `Paper.tsx`, `Privacy.tsx`, `Terms.tsx`, `Blog.tsx`, `CommitReviewArticle.tsx` — 12 usages) into a single `paperCard` recipe. Caught a subtle correctness issue before it shipped: both original classes declare `::before` on the *same* element, so they cascade together into one pseudo-element (later-declared `distressed-border` wins per-property, fully masking `paper-fold`'s gradient) — not two independent effects. Modeled the recipe as one `_before` matching that exact merged cascade rather than a naive `_before`+`_after`, which would've made the previously-invisible paper-fold gradient suddenly visible. Also repointed a print-media legal-doc override that targeted the old classnames.

**What's left in retro.css** is mostly single-page-only layout (Landing's hero/terminal/manifesto/install sections, marketing grids) that isn't repeated across files — lower value to convert since Panda's benefit is deduplication, and single-use layout CSS carries migration risk for no dedup payoff. Genuine remaining repeated-primitive candidates I saw but didn't touch: `font-terminal` (used in ~16 files including non-marketing pages, worth checking for the app-wide dead-usage oddity I noticed), and `prompt` (5 marketing files, deliberately left alone both times so far). Want me to keep going on either of those next?
